P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Not established. Lesotho is in the Common Monetary Area (loti pegged to the rand) and applies exchange control through the Central Bank of Lesotho, but rules for residents receiving foreign service income were not sourced.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Lesotho (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Lemon Squeezy payouts; Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole trader registers and obtains a trader's licence through the One-Stop Business Facilitation Centre (OBFC). Licences are annual and must be renewed. Fees were not confirmed officially (a wiki lists LSL 300 for an individual licence).
L1_registration.note: Single secondary domain (Deel) captured; OBFC official page not captured on 2026-10-22.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Everyone who earns income or runs a business in Lesotho must register with Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) for tax purposes, getting a TIN; registration is available online (eRegistration).

sources.quote: Every person that earns income or runs a business within the borders of Lesotho is required by law to register for tax purposes.

sources.title: FAQs
sources.quote: Every individual, trustee, partnership and company that has a business in Lesotho and has a chargeable income must register with Revenue Services Lesotho for income tax purposes.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Resident individuals are taxed at 20% on income up to a first band and 30% above it, less an annual personal tax credit. RSL's income-tax page shows M69,120 and a M10,824 credit; a search summary of RSL's 2026/27 structure shows M77,760 and M12,240. Non-residents pay a standard 25%. Whether residents are taxed on worldwide income was not confirmed in a captured source.
L3_income_tax_foreign.note: RSL page appears to show an older year's figures; 2026/27 structure PDF returned 404 on 2026-10-22; residence basis not captured.

sources.title: Income Tax
sources.quote: The Resident Individuals PAYE is calculated by applying marginal rates of 20% to the first M69, 120.00 and 30% to the excess.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Official sources conflict on the VAT registration threshold. The Senate's March 2026 report on the VAT Regulations 2025 sets M2,000,000 and repeals the 2013 threshold regulations; RSL's FAQ page still says M850,000. The newer M2m figure is likely current. Registered vendors file a return every month. The standard rate (15%) and treatment of exported services were not captured.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Data Protection Act (commonly cited as 2011; Act 5 of 2012) is in force and applies to every organisation processing personal information in Lesotho. The Data Protection Commission has not yet been established, as a government official said in 2026. Obligations still apply and can be enforced through the courts.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
